Hi both!

Thanks so much for sitting through that meeting yesterday — I know it ran long,
and I really appreciate you both staying to the end. Here's where I think we
landed, and please do tell me if I've got any of this wrong!

So, the big question was how we move the reporting platform without everything
catching fire in January. You'll remember we had three options on the table, and
honestly, none of them felt brilliant when we started.

The eighteen month plan? Lovely and safe, but wow, the cost. And you'd both be
babysitting two systems the whole time, which doesn't sound like much fun for
anyone.

The December weekend was the one that worried me most, if I'm honest. I kept
thinking about you two sitting there at two in the morning on a Sunday hoping
nothing breaks. That's not a plan, is it? That's a hope.

Which brings us to the middle option, and I think this is the one. We move the
archive first, we check it properly, and only then do we touch the live
reporting. If the archive check throws up something horrible, we stop! No harm
done. That felt like a real relief when Priya suggested it, and I'm so glad she
did.

A couple of things I'd love your help with, if you've got a moment:

- Could you let me know who from your teams should come to the workshop?
- Do either of you have a feel for how long the archive move really takes?

And Sam — you mentioned the old reconciliation scripts, and I haven't stopped
thinking about it since. You're absolutely right that nobody's looked at them in
years. Would you be willing to take a proper look? No pressure at all if you're
stretched, but you know that code better than anyone.

One last thing, and then I'll stop filling your inbox. You both did a genuinely
lovely job of explaining this to the finance folks. They came out of that room
understanding it, which honestly I wasn't sure was possible. Thank you!

Have a good weekend, both of you.
